# NJ08 Kotlin web source-map exclusion pilot

Status: isolated build/config candidate; **not NJ08 or product no-JSON acceptance**. Source baseline is `biome/full-port-2026@8c82b7a`, with Kotlin Gradle plugin 2.2.21 and Gradle 9.3.1 on macOS arm64. The unmodified local JS and Wasm distributions emitted `composeApp.js.map` JSON files with SHA-256 `5e99bc0dd081e26b2896c0d08b982e5c7143af8807db1d9a9dbfd8bc45e717db` and `64cd84b19fe24a17ae60ed0d68a67c4c3d54ee00571d1096649132eac5987a3f`. The [no-JSON ledger](NoJsonAcceptance.md) records the older compatibility output and the Pages copy path.

The Kotlin/JS target now sets `compilerOptions.sourceMap=false`; JS and Wasm browser Webpack configurations set `sourceMaps=false`. These are target/build settings, not product serialization or a new language layer. A `verifyNoWebSourceMaps` Gradle task depends on the compatibility distribution and rejects case-insensitive `.map` files in all three JS, Wasm and compatibility distribution directories. The existing CI preview and Pages workflow now call that task before upload/copy. [Kotlin's compiler-option reference](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/gradle-compiler-options.html) defines `sourceMap`; [Kotlin's browser setup reference](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/js-project-setup.html) describes Webpack configuration and the distribution tasks. No application-authored JSON was added.

From this isolated worktree's `kotlin/`, `./gradlew :composeApp:composeCompatibilityBrowserDistribution --console=plain --max-workers=2` passed: 106/106 actionable tasks executed in 1m39s. The fresh JS, Wasm and compatibility distribution directories contain 53 files combined and **zero filenames ending `.map` or `.json`**. The compatibility directory contains 21 files; its `originJsComposeApp.js` SHA-256 is `e1f889c7d1092ba03d80e68f3b375d27c007ab8b0f810e683ad538426c329a1e`, equal to the JS branch bundle, and `originWasmComposeApp.js` SHA-256 is `1acf75fb5aa08287ece9770985e5727967079d6c61d068a045cb02e3740559c7`, equal to the Wasm branch bundle. The app Wasm and shared Skiko Wasm remain distinct; this pilot does not assert that either executed in a browser.

`./gradlew :composeApp:verifyNoWebSourceMaps --console=plain --max-workers=2` passed on the same output (107 actionable tasks, 12 executed/95 up-to-date, 41s). An empty disposable `negative-control.MAP` placed only in the compatibility output made the task fail with the exact path; after deleting it, a rerun passed. The two control runs excluded the upstream distribution task only to avoid its recopy masking the injected file. The marker was not JSON and was removed; `git diff --check` passed. This establishes that the guard observes the intended output, not a full content scanner.

Limits: the current JS bundle still contains `application/json` paths from the old product, and fresh startup still writes legacy JSON; browser UI and the full NJ08 bundle/storage/export scan remain **NOT RUN**. The copied third-party `rive/rive.js` still has a dangling `sourceMappingURL=rive.js.map` comment although no map file is distributed, and contains its own `JSON.parse` at line 458; the final network/content audit must classify those uses. Kotlin's internal `composeApp/build/compileSync/wasmJs/.../*.wasm.map` files are still produced as ignored compiler intermediates (153,553 bytes each), and tool/test caches elsewhere also contain source maps. The current Pages workflow additionally builds and copies the old React app under `/react/`; this pilot guards only the three Kotlin distributions and does not satisfy the Kotlin-only cutover. The task only prevents source-map files in those distributions, and no live Pages deployment was performed. Do not count this as a literal zero-JSON application until all active product JSON and final artifact/runtime paths are removed and checked.
